items.title: Kalyn Ponga's Origin send-off leaves Queensland legend 'in shock'
items.description: Maroons great Darren Lockyer says the decision to send off Kalyn Ponga late in State of Origin will be hard to accept for Queenslanders.

items.title: ISIS-linked woman barred from Australia tried to board flight
items.description: An Australian woman with links to ISIS, who is barred from Australia on a temporary exclusion order, tried to board a flight home with the other members of Tuesday's returning cohort, a Senate estimates hearing has been told.

items.title: Trump says US 'not satisfied' with Iran peace deal proposals
items.description: It comes as the White House rejects a draft deal being reported by Iranian state TV as a "fabrication".

items.title: Video shows divers finding five Lao cavers alive, two remain missing
items.description: A rescue mission has been underway for more than a week to find seven people who entered a cave in central Laos before becoming trapped in a landslide triggered by heavy rain.

items.title: UK spy chief says West between peace and war, as Russia ramps up cyberattacks
items.description: The head of a major UK intelligence agency is warning that Moscow and other adversaries could use artificial intelligence and other emerging technology to conduct "hybrid warfare" against western allies.

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket are billion dollar bets banned from Australia — for now
items.description: Kalshi and Polymarket have gone from obscure start-ups to two of the world's biggest prediction markets where users bet on yes-or-no questions spanning politics, pop culture and war.

items.title: FIFA faces investigation over World Cup's 'impossibly high' ticket prices
items.description: In a joint statement, New Jersey's attorney-general accused the football governing body of having turned "buying a ticket to the World Cup into a gauntlet of confusion, fake scarcity, and impossibly high prices".

items.title: Bondi shooting victim labelled 'subhuman' in online abuse of inquiry witnesses
items.description: Victims of antisemitism have been targeted with death threats and depicted as animals in AI-generated images after giving evidence to the royal commission examining the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: PM response to truth-telling process 'hugely significant'
items.description: The Walk for Truth ended at Parliament House today and while there was not a firm commitment from the PM, many felt the response was a 'positive move'.

items.title: Labor MP defends electoral registration to empty block amid rebuild
items.description: Dickson MP Ali France has been referred to the Australian Electoral Commission with claims she is registered to vote at a vacant suburban block in her north Brisbane electorate.

items.title: What we know, and what we don't, about new changes to Centrelink system
items.description: The federal government has proposed changes to Australia's $2 billion employment services system to make them “more responsive, effective and dignified”.

items.title: This 24yo started gambling as a teenager and has now lost 900k
items.description: From footy tips to Taylor Swift bets, teenagers are being lured into gambling. Almost 34 per cent of Australian teenagers gamble and everyone from teachers, experts, to the young people themselves are sounding the alarm.

items.title: Multiple crime scenes declared after man dies in Childers area
items.description: One man is dead and two others are in hospital, as police declare multiple crime scenes in a regional Queensland town.

items.title: Russia looks for new soldiers in Transnistria as war casualty numbers grow
items.description: The Kremlin is trying to recruit more soldiers for its war in Ukraine but an analyst says at the rate of casualties, "Russia cannot replace recruits fast enough to keep the 'meat grinder' fed."

items.title: Cuts of meat that will give you more bang for your buck
items.description: If you are looking to trim your household food budget, lower-cost cuts of meat could be a good place to start. Here are some tips on what to look for and how to cook them.

items.title: Chalmers flags 'legitimate' small business CGT debate
items.description: The government is treading carefully on carve-outs to its capital gains tax legislation amid backlash to its plan.

items.title: ABC's Justin Stevens resigns as director of news
items.description: Justin Stevens, the ABC's director of news, has announced his resignation after 19 years with the organisation.

items.title: Bulk carrier rescues two fishermen and Smokey the dog after boat sinks
items.description: An emergency distress beacon activation off the North Queensland coast yesterday afternoon sparked a coordinated rescue involving a bulk carrier and rescue jet.

items.title: Police say cause of Kumanjayi White's death in custody still not known
items.description: The Northern Territory police commissioner says the cause of 24-year-old Kumanjayi White's death in custody remains undetermined, with the criminal case against the officers who restrained him now closed.

items.title: Why Blak Douglas won't enter the Archibald Prize again
items.description: The acclaimed Dunghutti artist is using his latest exhibition to challenge perceptions of Aboriginal art and the systemic issues creatives face in Australia.

items.title: More or Less quiz: We need you to rank five State of Origin greats
items.description: If you think you know your stuff when it comes to State of Origin, here's your chance to prove it.

items.title: Inquest hears NDIS provider delayed suicide threat reports before teen's death
items.description: The inquest in Southport is examining whether any deficiencies in the boy's care or accommodation caused or contributed to his death.

items.title: Record-breaking rain welcomed in drought-hit parts of NSW
items.description: Up to 100 millimetres of rain has been welcomed across drought-hit parts of western NSW, but some farmers expecting relief were left disappointed.

items.title: Rodent faeces, animal blood, mould spark $60k penalty for country bakery
items.description: Inspectors found animal blood dripping onto bread, rodent faeces on food and spreading mould at the Albany French Hot Bread Shop, triggering prosecution and $60,000 in penalties for the owners.

items.title: Bystanders foil alleged kidnap attempt of woman changing tyre in Sydney
items.description: A 27-year-old woman was changing a tyre when a man allegedly threatened her with a knife and attempted to drag her into an SUV, NSW Police said.
